owned.description: True if the user owns this game, false if they have said they don't; omitted when not set

format.description: How the user has the game. Known values are 'physical', 'digital', and 'other'; omitted when not set

replay.description: Points to the original playthrough record if this is a replay

status.description: Collection status. Canonical values are 'playing', 'wishlisted', 'backlogged', and 'played'; the remaining known values are legacy and only appear in older records ('started' → playing, 'wishlist' → wishlisted, 'shelved' → backlogged, 'finished'/'abandoned' → played with a playedStatus)

isReplay.description: True if this entry represents a replay of a previously played game

playtime.description: Time the user has played the game, in minutes, as they entered it; omitted when not set

resumedAt.description: Set when a shelved or finished game is moved back to 'playing'; distinguishes a resume from an initial start

updatedAt.description: When the entry's status last changed, including a sub-status change such as backlogged to shelved or playing to endless. Not bumped by details-only edits

playedStatus.description: How a played game concluded. Canonical values are 'completed', 'mastered', 'retired', and 'abandoned'; 'shelved' is legacy and only appears in older records

librarySource.description: Free-text store or service the game is kept on, e.g. 'Steam' or 'Nintendo eShop'

playingStatus.description: Refines a 'playing' status; 'endless' means a game with no finish line (multiplayer, live service) that the user keeps coming back to. Shown as 'Ongoing'

backloggedStatus.description: Refines a 'backlogged' status; 'shelved' means the game was started but is paused for now

main.description: A game in a user's collection

releaseDate.description: Release date as a Unix timestamp in seconds, sourced from IGDB

status.description: The primary status the entry moved to. The sub-status (playedStatus, backloggedStatus, playingStatus) is on the record itself.

statusChange.description: Present only on the write that set the entry's status: when it was added, or when it moved to a different primary status (playing, played, backlogged, wishlisted). Any later write that doesn't change the status removes it, and imports never set it. Lets automations (e.g. Airglow) react once to a start or a finish instead of to every edit of the entry.

atUri.description: AT URI to a canonical game record on a shared game database
